# Test: shared mineral kill-drop rule

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC3, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic unit + guard tests that pin the contract of the shared mineral kill-drop rule **before** it is implemented, so `PlayScene` and the gyms provably share one rule.

## Required coverage

- Small asteroid (`getSizeTier() === 'small'`) → exactly one mineral drop at the asteroid's death position.
- Large and medium asteroid → no direct drop (their small split children drop).
- Non-asteroid enemy that absorbed N minerals → re-drops between `mineralRedropFractionMin` and `mineralRedropFractionMax` of N, never more than N, at the death site, using a seeded RNG for determinism.
- Non-asteroid enemy with 0 absorbed minerals → no drops.
- Re-drop scatter stays within `MINERAL_REDROP_SCATTER_RADIUS` of the death site.

## Assumption

Shared helper module path: `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` exporting `resolveMineralKillDrops(scene, entity, rng): Mineral[]` (operator selected the shared-helper approach — see the parent item's Appendix).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid drop + non-asteroid re-drop) has one production definition that both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` consume, and a repo-wide guard asserts it.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New tests cover the shared rule and the guard; `npm test` for the new files passes.
- The unit tests are deterministic (seeded RNG, no reliance on `Math.random`) and cover every bullet under Required coverage.
- Tests fail before the implementation task lands and pass once it does.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.test.ts` — new.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend guard.
- `src/test/duplicateBodyGuard.ts` — shared guard helper (extend if needed).
- `src/entities/__tests__/BaseEnemy.minerals.test.ts` — keep green / extend.

# Shared player-control step across all scenes

**Parent:** `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` (register gap 1 & 11).

## Summary

The sequence *input → tick weapon timers → apply P5 speed/fire-rate multipliers → physics → auto-fire* is re-implemented in `PlayScene.tick`, `GymFormationScene.tick`, `GymWeapons.tick`, `GymPowerUpsUtility.tick` and `GymPowerUpsCombat.tick`, and `GymPlayer.update` inlines the scheme→input mapping instead of the shared `_readPlayerInput`. Extract one `_tickPlayer(dt)` (and keep `_readPlayerInput`) in `CombatCoreScene` so every scene advances the player identically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** — `CombatCoreScene` owns a single `_tickPlayer(dt)` that performs, in the same order every frame: `tickWeaponTimers`, live `setSpeedMultiplier`/`setFireRateMultiplier` from the effects registry, `_readPlayerInput`→`setInput`, `physicsTick`, and `_autoFire`. `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymWeapons` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` call it instead of their local copy. Answer (epic `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`): *Recommended: consume the shared input/physics helper; it need not add enemies.* Final accepted: **yes** — AC2 requires `GymPlayer` to consume the shared input mapping.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Is the sequence described in the summary actually one identical sequence in every named scene?" Recorded as an implementation assumption; if a test shows a behaviour change in those gyms the difference must be recorded in the epic and approved.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Does `GymPowerUpsCombat` use a fake fixed 16 ms clock for the *player* path (AC4)?" # Intake Brief — Make P9 Magnet timed on pickup and permanent-stack on upgrade (AH-0MUTOTLCY005NZ8L)

**Headline:** Bring the **P9 Magnet** into line with the **P10 Mineral Scoop** hybrid model — a **15 s, refresh-only** timed drop-attraction for field pickups and a **permanent stacking (cap 5)** attraction for the hold-full upgrade — implemented once in the shared `EffectsRegistry` so the game and every gym run identical behaviour.

## Problem statement

The P9 Magnet is currently **always** a permanent stack (cap 5): every pickup, whether a field drop or a hold-full reward, permanently increases the attraction radius. The P10 Mineral Scoop (AH-0MUPMR9TX00756BQ) introduced a hybrid model — timed on field pickup, permanent-stacking on upgrade — and the operator requested during that intake that P9 be brought into line for design consistency. Until this change the two attraction power-ups share a radius curve but not the same duration/stacking semantics, which is an inconsistency the player can feel and the docs must paper over.

## Users

- **Player** — wants a predictable, escalating reward loop: a temporary convenience from a field drop, and a permanent, stacking boon from a deliberate hold-full choice.
- **Developer** — wants the magnet's timed/permanent behaviour defined once in the shared `EffectsRegistry` and consumed by every scene, so the game and gyms cannot drift.

Example user stories:

- As a player, when I collect a **P9 Magnet** field drop, nearby drops drift toward my ship for **15 s** so pickups are easier; re-collecting refreshes the timer to full.
- As a player, when I choose P9 as a **hold-full reward**, the drop attraction becomes a permanent part of my run, so I never lose the convenience.
- As a developer, the magnet's timed/permanent behaviour is modelled once in the shared registry and every scene consumes the same effective-stacks accessor, so the game and gyms run identical code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Field pickup is a timed, refreshing effect.** `applyCollect('P9')` (the field-drop path, no `permanent` flag) activates a **15 s** drop-attraction effect; re-collecting refreshes the timer to full and **does not** add permanent stacks. Verified by unit tests in `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` (activation, expiry after 15 s, refresh, no permanent stack).
- [ ] **Hold-full upgrade is a permanent stacking effect.** `applyCollect('P9', true)` (the `applyMineralChoiceReward` path) grants a **permanent** attraction that stacks up to **5** and never decays on `tick`. Verified by unit tests in `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` / `src/powerups/__tests__/effects.permanent.test.ts`.
- [ ] **One shared effective-stacks accessor drives attraction.** A `magnetEffectStacks()` accessor (mirroring the existing `scoopEffectStacks()`) returns the permanent stack count when any upgrade was chosen, otherwise **1** while the timed field pickup is active, otherwise **0**. `CombatCoreScene._applyDropMagnet` consumes it, so `PlayScene` and every gym pull drops with identical range semantics; the repo-wide duplicate-body/equivalence parity guard stays green.
- [ ] **Help copy and documentation reflect the hybrid model.** The `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.P9` description, GDD §4.4 table/notes and README power-up list describe P9 as "15 s timed pickup / permanent stacking when chosen as a reward (cap 5)", matching the P10 wording style.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Parity rule (AGENTS.md):** shared behaviour lives once in `src/powerups/` and `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by both the game and the gyms; no divergent copy. The duplicate-body guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and the gym-parity docs assertion must stay green. Only a *disabled* feature may differ.
- **Duration (operator decision, parent intake Q1/Q5):** field pickup is **15 s**, refresh-only.
- **Timed radius (documented assumption):** while only the timed effect is active, use the minimum active radius — the equivalent of **one magnet stack** (`magnetRadius(shipSize, 1)` = `1 × 20 × 1.5` = **30 px** at `SHIP_SIZE = 20`), mirroring the P10 decision. Permanent stacks (≥ 1) define the radius when present. (Non-blocking; see Open questions.)
- **Single radius curve:** `magnetRadius(shipSize, stacks)` remains the one source of truth for both P9 and P10 (`mineralScoopRadius` delegates to it) — do not fork or change its signature/semantics.
- **Cap stays 5:** `P9_MAX_STACKS` remains the permanent-stack cap; the timed path never stacks.
- **No new activation key:** the magnet stays passive.
- **Existing-test ripple:** today many tests call `applyCollect('P9')` (no flag) expecting permanent stacks (`src/ui/HUD.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, scene and gym tests). These must be updated to the **permanent** path (`applyCollect('P9', true)`) wherever they intend the upgrade, and the timed path covered by new tests. This is expected work, not a regression.

## Existing state

- `EffectsRegistry` (`src/powerups/effects.ts`) already models the P10 hybrid: `_scoopStacks`, `P10_MAX_STACKS`, `P10_SCOOP_DURATION = 15`, `isScoopActive()`, `scoopEffectStacks()`, and a `MINERAL_SCOOP` case that branches on `permanent`. The P9 `MAGNET` case currently **ignores** `permanent` and always increments `_magnetStacks` (cap `P9_MAX_STACKS`).
- `magnetRadius(shipSize, stacks)` returns `MAGNET_RADIUS_BASE_MULTIPLIER (1) × shipSize × (1 + MAGNET_RADIUS_PER_STACK (0.5) × stacks)`. `mineralScoopRadius` delegates to it.
- `CombatCoreScene._applyDropMagnet` calls `applyDropMagnet(..., getEffectsRegistry().magnetStacks(), dt)` — the permanent-stack count only.
- The hold-full reward path (`applyMineralChoiceReward`, `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`) calls `effectsRegistry.applyCollect(option.id, true)` for power-up options; the field-drop path (`CombatCoreScene._collectDrop`) calls `applyCollect(dropId)` with no flag.
- `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.P9` (`src/powerups/types.ts`) has description "Permanently pulls nearby drops toward the ship (stacks up to 5)." and no `duration`; P10 carries `duration: 15` + `maxStacks: 5`.
- `activeEffects()` surfaces P9 permanent stacks as an `xN` row when `_magnetStacks > 0`; timed P10 surfaces from `_timed` plus a stack row (never `x0`). HUD `formatValue` renders `Ns` for timed rows and `xN` for stack rows.
- Existing tests assuming field-pickup permanence include `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` (`P9 Magnet (AC4)`), `src/ui/HUD.test.ts` (HUD AC2), and scene/gym/drop-layer/equivalence tests that collect P9.

## Desired change

Make P9 a hybrid exactly analogous to P10:

- **Registry:** add `P9_MAGNET_DURATION = 15`; branch the `MAGNET` case on `permanent` (permanent → +1 stack capped at 5; field pickup → timed `_timed` entry, refresh-only); add `isMagnetActive()` and `magnetEffectStacks()`; include the timed P9 row and permanent P9 stack row (never `x0`) in `activeEffects()`; reset both states in `reset()`.
- **Scene wiring:** `CombatCoreScene._applyDropMagnet` consumes `magnetEffectStacks()` instead of `magnetStacks()`.
- **Catalogue:** add `duration: 15` to `P9` and rewrite its description to the hybrid wording.
- **Docs:** update GDD §4.4 (P9 row + notes) and README power-up/effects descriptions; remove the "tracked separately" note where it refers to this now-delivered change.
- **Tests:** extend `effects.test.ts` (timed activation/expiry/refresh, permanent stacking/cap, `magnetEffectStacks()`, `activeEffects()` shape, `reset()`), migrate existing field-pickup-as-permanent assertions to the permanent path, and keep parity/HUD/scene tests green.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `P9_MAGNET_DURATION`, hybrid `MAGNET` case, `isMagnetActive()`, `magnetEffectStacks()`, `activeEffects()`, `reset()`; doc-comment updates.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — `P9` catalogue `duration: 15` + hybrid description.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `_applyDropMagnet` uses `magnetEffectStacks()`.
- `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` — timed/permanent P9 unit tests (mirroring the P10 block).
- `src/powerups/__tests__/effects.permanent.test.ts` — permanent-path coverage if applicable.
- `src/ui/HUD.test.ts` — migrate P9 stack assertions to the permanent path; add a timed-row case.
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — effective-stacks pull + parity guard.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts` — scene-level P9 semantics/parity.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 P9 row + notes.
- `README.md` — power-up / shared-effects descriptions.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the timed/permanent split maps cleanly onto the existing `applyCollect(id, permanent)` flag, exactly as it did for P10. *Mitigation:* registry unit tests for both paths before scene wiring.
- **Risk — behavioural change ripples through existing tests.** Many tests use `applyCollect('P9')` to mean "permanent stack". *Mitigation:* systematically migrate those assertions to `applyCollect('P9', true)` and add explicit timed-path tests; the full suite must be green before `in_review`.
- **Risk — HUD dual timed/stacked display.** P9 changes type between pickups and upgrades; a stale `×0` would mislead. *Mitigation:* only surface stacks/remaining when active, mirroring P10's zero-suppression rule; add a HUD test.
- **Risk — parity drift.** If any scene computes its own stacks or radius, gyms diverge. *Mitigation:* one accessor (`magnetEffectStacks()`), shared `_applyDropMagnet`, and the duplicate-body/equivalence guard.
- **Risk — radius-curve coupling with P10.** `magnetRadius` is shared with the scoop; a careless change would alter P10. *Mitigation:* leave `magnetRadius` untouched and reuse it.
- **Assumption:** reusing the existing P9 pickup cue unchanged is acceptable; no new SFX required.
- **Assumption:** a timed P9 field pickup does **not** clear or cancel an existing permanent upgrade (and vice versa); the effective radius is driven by permanent stacks when present. Mirrors P10.
- **Scope-creep risk:** any generic "attractor target predicate" refactor or further P10 changes are out of scope; record extra opportunities as linked work items, not scope.

Final accepted answer: field pickup = **timed**, hold-full upgrade = **permanent stacking**. Source: interactive reply recorded in AH-0MUPMR9TX00756BQ (`AH-C0MUQCYKT0000D52H`); the discovered-from work item is this item. The seed context supplied in the description therefore suffices to draft the brief, per the intake skill's "skip the interview when the seed context suffices" rule.

# Switch game audio from procedural Web Audio to ToneForge

## Problem statement

Replace the game's hand-rolled procedural Web Audio synthesis (~2,253 lines in `src/audio/effects.ts`) with **ToneForge** (`../ToneForge`) — build-time rendered WAV assets consumed via Phaser. All SFX are produced through one dedicated audio toolchain, ensuring reproducible, seed-deterministic output.

## Decision: Baked assets (approach A)

**Chosen approach: Build-time baked WAV assets.** ToneForge CLI renders each cue to a WAV file during a build step, consumed by Phaser at runtime. This matches ToneForge's documented game-dev workflow, keeps the browser dependency surface clean (no Node-only deps leaking into the game bundle), and is the simplest integration path.

**Trade-off:** Runtime variation (pitch jitter, thrust-driven hum) is lost in baked form. These are handled separately:
- Thruster hum: baked multiple variants or played via a lightweight Tone.js shim at runtime (to be evaluated in a follow-up work item).
- Pitch jitter: baked multiple variants with different seeds to approximate variation.

**Child work items created:**
- Make ToneForge Runtime-aware (browser-compatible) — sibling work item in `../ToneForge`
- Consider switching to runtime generation when possible — child work item here
- Update ToneForge license to MIT — sibling work item in `../ToneForge`

## Users

- **Game developer (primary):** Wants a single, well-documented audio toolchain with deterministic output, easy recipe authoring, and reproducible builds.

### User stories

- As the game's developer, I want every SFX cue produced via ToneForge so that audio is authored, generated and varied reproducibly with one toolchain.
- As the game's developer, I want the build pipeline to render all WAV assets in CI so that the game bundle is self-contained and reproducible.
- As the game's developer, I want to author new recipes in ToneForge without modifying game audio code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Approach recorded:** Baked assets (A) approach is chosen with rationale; any required ToneForge changes are split into child work items (runtime-awareness, licence update, future runtime consideration).
- **Cue-to-recipe mapping:** Every cue exported by `src/audio/effects.ts` today is mapped to a ToneForge recipe/stack/sequence (existing or newly authored) or explicitly retired, documented on this item.
- **Recipes in ToneForge:** Any newly authored recipes/presets live in `../ToneForge` and are documented there (name, character, seed).
- **Audible character preserved (verification step):** The audible character of each retained cue matches GDD §7.3 (waveform family, frequency contour and nominal volume preserved within audible similarity), verified by the explicit audible-character audition step in Author game-specific ToneForge recipes (AH-0MUTYV8480019Z51).
- **Global volume/mute:** `setSfxVolume`/`setSfxMuted` continues to affect all cues; SettingsScene controls still work.
- **Single shared context:** Exactly one shared `AudioContext` is created; a new scene/cue does not construct a second context (invariant asserted in tests).
- **No-op when unavailable:** In an environment without an `AudioContext`, every cue degrades to a no-op and never throws (verified by headless tests).
- **Advance cues ≥ 500 ms:** Advance cues remain ≥ 500 ms and cue→fire scheduling remains gap-free where required.
- **Deterministic build:** Rendering is seed-deterministic, checksums are recorded, and the generation step is reproducible in CI.
- **Pinned dependency:** ToneForge is consumed reproducibly (`file:` dependency to sibling checkout, pinned to a commit or tag); the build must not silently depend on an unpinned checkout.
- **No Node-only deps in browser:** Node-only ToneForge dependencies do not leak into the browser game bundle.
- **Tests and build pass:** Full test suite passes (`npm test`), and `npm run build` / `npm run typecheck` pass clean.
- **Documentation updated:** GDD §7.3, the audio-directory tree note and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` describe the ToneForge-based pipeline.

## Constraints

- GDD §7.3 currently mandates "zero external audio assets" — the baked approach changes this stance; the GDD must be updated to reflect build-time generation.
- ToneForge is v0.1.0; API may change. Pin to a specific commit/tag.
- ToneForge license must be resolved (MIT — child work item in sibling repo).
- Build-time generation must be reproducible (deterministic seeds, checksums).
- The thruster hum is continuous and thrust-driven — may need a runtime shim or multiple baked variants.

## Existing state

- ~2,253 lines of procedural Web Audio in `src/audio/effects.ts`
- Consumers import cue functions directly from `../audio/effects`
- ToneForge sibling checkout at `../ToneForge` (commit `c48fed5`, MIT license — TBD in repo)

- Build pipeline step renders all game cues to WAV via ToneForge CLI

- SettingsScene volume/mute controls wired to Phaser audio node
- Tests updated to assert ToneForge-based behaviour

# Deterministic WAV build pipeline

## Goal

Create a build step that renders every game recipe to baked WAV assets under `public/audio/sfx/` via the ToneForge CLI, with recorded checksums, so the game bundle is self-contained and the generation step is reproducible in CI.

As the game's developer, I want the build pipeline to render all WAV assets in CI so that the game bundle is self-contained and reproducible.

## Scope

- Add `scripts/build-audio.sh` that iterates the game recipe manifest, invokes `tf generate --recipe <slug> --seed <n> --output public/audio/sfx/<name>.wav`, and fails fast on any render error.
- Emit `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` (SHA-256 per asset) after a successful render.
- Add an `npm run build-audio` script and wire it into `npm run build` as a preceding step.
- Add a reproducibility check: re-rendering with the same seeds must reproduce identical checksums; drift fails the script.
- Add a CI step that runs `npm run build-audio` and fails if generated assets differ from the committed checksums.
- Handle pitch-jitter variants (explosions) by rendering a small fixed set of seeds and selecting among them at runtime.
- Thruster hum is out of scope for baking (handled by the runtime shim task).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `npm run build-audio` renders all manifest recipes to `public/audio/sfx/` and exits non-zero on any failure.
- `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` records a SHA-256 for every rendered asset.
- Re-running `npm run build-audio` with unchanged seeds produces an identical `checksums.json`.
- `npm run build` invokes the audio build before the Vite bundle step.
- CI fails when a rendered asset's checksum does not match the committed manifest.
- The script's recipe manifest is a single source of truth consumed by both the build and the tests.
- No Node-only ToneForge dependency is bundled into the browser output (verified by build inspection).

## Dependencies

- Author game-specific ToneForge recipes (must exist before they can be rendered).

## Deliverables

- `scripts/build-audio.sh`.
- Recipe manifest file consumed by the script.
- `public/audio/sfx/` baked WAV assets plus `checksums.json`.
- `package.json` `build-audio` script and `build` wiring.
- CI job step invoking the build and verifying checksums.

# Mortar detonates at a random point within weapon range (no forward projectile)

## Problem statement
The Mortar currently fires a slow shell forward in the ship's facing direction, detonating after ~1 s or on enemy/bullet contact (effective range ≈ 180 px). The operator requires it instead to **detonate at a random location within its defined range on fire** — no travelling projectile, no forward bias, no collision tracking.

## Users
- **Player:** Wants a strategic-area-denial tool that can engage enemies around the ship (behind it, to the side) without needing to aim. Affects gameplay by shifting Mortar from "aimed burst" to "area randomisation" — useful for clearing bullets near the ship or surprising enemies.
- **Testers / QA:** Need deterministic test paths for random detonation, off-screen visual culling, and sound playback.

## Existing state
- Mortar is an `'onImpact'` AOE weapon (GDD §6.4, `src/utils/weapons.ts`): spawns a projectile at `projectileSpeed` (180 px/s) in the ship's facing direction; projectile detonates via `onExpire` / collision path.
- Dispatch: `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` spawns a bullet tagged `aoeWeapon`; `CombatScene.onAoeProjectileSpawned` attaches `onExpire`; collisions/expiry call `detonateAoeProjectile` → `applyAoeEffect` + `spawnAoeDetonationVfx`.
- Blast radius = 35 px. VFX = `spawnMortarBurst`. SFX = `playMortarDetonationSound` (always fires).
- `AOE_RADII.mortar = 35`, `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS.mortar = 180`, `WEAPON_BULLET_LIFETIME.mortar = 1.0` → effective range = 180 px.
- GDD §6.4 describes "travels in the ship's facing direction and detonates on impact or expiry".

## Desired change
- On fire, the Mortar resolves its AOE **instantly** at N random points within its defined range (N = `def.offsets.length` after `projectileCount` leveling), instead of spawning a projectile.
- The range used for the randomisation is the weapon's existing effective range: `def.aoe.projectileSpeed × def.bulletLifetime` (180 px at level 0; scaled by the `bulletLifetime` upgrade multiplier).
- Random point distribution: area-uniform over the disc of radius `range` centred on the ship (any direction).
- If a random point falls outside the play bounds (`[0, width] × [0, height]`): **audio still plays** (detonation cue fires), but **VFX is skipped** (no off-screen graphics).
- The generic `'onImpact'` projectile-detonation machinery remains in place (unused by the Mortar after this change, but not removed — dead code retained per project discipline).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1 — No Mortar projectile.** After the change, firing the Mortar spawns **zero** travelling player bullets. `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts` verifies no bullet is created on auto-fire of the Mortar.
- [ ] **AC2 — Random detonation at fire time.** Mortar resolves its AOE effect at a random point within its defined range (computed as `aoe.projectileSpeed × def.bulletLifetime`). At least one AOE effect is present immediately after firing. `AoeWeapons.test.ts` verifies this with a deterministic RNG.
- [ ] **AC3 — Multiple detonations for leveled weapons.** When `projectileCount` leveling increases `def.offsets.length` beyond 1, the number of random detonations per fire equals `def.offsets.length`. Test: leveled Mortar (e.g. 2 extra projectiles) produces exactly 3 detonation effects.
- [ ] **AC4 — Off-screen handling.** When a random point falls outside the play area: `playMortarDetonationSound` still fires; `spawnMortarBurst` is not called (or the VFX is not added). Test verifies sound fires and no VFX graphics are created for that detonation.
- [ ] **AC5 — AOE effect correctness.** The effect applies correctly: damages enemies inside the blast radius and clears enemy bullets. `AoeWeapons.test.ts` verifies enemy/bullet effects are correct for random detonation points.
- [ ] **AC6 — Gym↔game parity.** `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` passes — the game and every gym inherit the same behaviour. No new non-shared AOE methods are introduced on non-core scenes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4 A2 table updated to remove "travels in the ship's facing direction" and reflect the random detonation behaviour. `src/aoeDocs.test.ts` still passes (the GDD still documents AOE trigger semantics).
- [ ] **AC8 — Unit tests.** Pure random-point helper (`aoe.ts`) has unit tests. The Mortar random-detonation path has integration tests in `AoeWeapons.test.ts`.

- [ ] **AC9 — Full suite green.** `npm test` (full project suite) passes with the new changes, and `npx tsc --noEmit` typechecks cleanly.

## Constraints
- No travelling projectile is spawned; no `aoeWeapon` tag on bullets (for the Mortar).
- Random point distribution must be area-uniform over the disc (not uniform over angle × distance).
- Audio always fires regardless of detonation point position.
- Dead code discipline: the existing `'onImpact'` machinery (`onAoeProjectileSpawned`, `detonateAoeProjectile`, `bullet.aoeWeapon`, `bullet.aoeDetonated`) remains in place.
- Design decision: introduce a new `AoETrigger` value `'onRandom'` (union becomes `'onFire' | 'onImpact' | 'onRandom'`). `'onImpact'` remains for potential future weapons.

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Risk:** The `AoETrigger` union type change touches `weapons.ts`, `CombatCoreScene.ts`, and `CombatScene.ts`. Mitigation: small, well-tested change.
- **Risk:** Existing F3 tests in `AoeWeapons.test.ts` are all about the travelling projectile — most will need rewriting. Mitigation: keep the `detonateAoeProjectile` tests (they test effect logic, not spawn path) and rewrite the projectile-specific ones.
- **Assumption:** `projectileCount` leveling for Mortar (which increases `def.offsets.length`) correctly maps to "number of random detonations" rather than "projectiles per shot".
- **Scope-creep risk:** Adding `randomPlacement` or `randomRange` fields to `AoEDescriptor` is unnecessary — the range is derived from existing fields. Keeping it simple avoids descriptor bloat.
- **GDD test risk:** `src/aoeDocs.test.ts` asserts GDD matches `/onImpact/`. Since `'onImpact'` remains in the type union, the GDD can still document it alongside `'onFire'` and `'onRandom'`. No test change expected.

## Key Files (predicted)
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `AoETrigger` union extended to include `'onRandom'`; Mortar descriptor uses `'onRandom'`; docs updated.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `_autoFire`: handle `'onRandom'` → skip bullet, call `onAoeRandomFired`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `onAoeRandomFired`: pick N random points, resolve effect at each; `spawnAoeDetonationVfx`: off-screen VFX culling; `onAoeFired` delegates to `onAoeRandomFired` for `'onRandom'`.
- `src/utils/aoe.ts` — Pure helper: `selectRandomPoint(centre, range, rng)` for area-uniform disc sampling (testable).
- `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts` — Rewrite F3 tests: no projectile spawn, random detonation at fire time, off-screen handling.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — Parity guard: `onAoeRandomFired` must be on shared core prototype.
- `src/aoeDocs.test.ts` — GDD still documents `'onImpact'` and `'onFire'` triggers (they remain in the type union); no change needed.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — A2 Mortar entry updated to reflect random detonation.
- `src/utils/weapons.test.ts` — Trigger assertion for Mortar updated to `'onRandom'`.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` — `'onImpact'` comments retained (dead code note).

## Related work
- **F3: Mortar weapon — onImpact detonation (AH-0MUQUSFXB007NSLN):** Current implementation — spawns and tracks projectile.
- **F1: AOE core infrastructure (AH-0MUOOB3OR001V8CD):** Generic AOE dispatch and descriptor model.
- **F6: Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUQUYHY0000MZ2F):** Shared hook inheritance model.
- **F7: Documentation and full suite validation (AH-0MUQUC14P006F6SH):** Docs and test guard.
- **Weapon leveling (AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J):** `projectileCount` and `bulletLifetime` upgrades that must continue to apply.
- **AOE weapons description (AH-0MUOOB3OR001V8CD):** Parent epic defining the AOE trigger model.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (idempotent)

- Q: What defines the "range" that bounds the random detonation point? — **Answer (operator, intake round 1):** A) The mortar's existing effective range (projectileSpeed × bulletLifetime = 180 px), scaled by the bulletLifetime upgrade multiplier. **Recommended option selected.** Source: interactive reply.
- Q: How should the random point be distributed? — **Answer (operator, intake round 1):** A) Uniform over the disc of radius `range` centred on the ship (any direction, area-uniform). **Recommended option selected.** Source: interactive reply.
- Q: If a random point falls outside the visible play area (ship near an edge)? — **Answer (operator, intake round 1):** B) Allow off-screen detonations (effect still applies). Audio still fires, visuals can be skipped. Source: interactive reply.

# Intake Brief — Wire power-up level curves into EffectsRegistry and the shared effect path (AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K)

**Headline:** Consume the shipped `resolvePowerUpAtLevel()` / `PowerUpLevelStore`
inside `EffectsRegistry` and the single shared effect path so every power-up
collection (field pickup or hold-full reward) advances exactly one run-scoped
level, effect strength is resolved from the catalogue instead of raw tuning
constants, and the existing stack/charge/lives state is derived from the level
model with no second counter — identically in `PlayScene` and every gym.

**Status:** intake **paused** — 2 producer decisions required (see
[Open questions](#appendix-clarifying-questions--answers)). The brief below is
complete and actionable apart from the two marked decisions.

## Seed context (verbatim from the work item)

> Follow-on from AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 (design + catalogue + pure resolver +
> integration contract). Consume `resolvePowerUpAtLevel()`/`PowerUpLevelStore`
> inside `EffectsRegistry` and the shared effect path so every power-up
> collection levels the power-up up (run-scoped, persists across activation
> timeouts, resets on run restart), and existing stack/charge state (P9/P10
> stacks, P7 stacks, P6 charges, P8 lives) is derived from the level model with
> no double-counting. Must run the same code in `PlayScene` and every gym
> (gym<->game parity, AGENTS.md) and replace the raw tuning constants with
> resolved stats. `discovered-from:AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6`

## Problem statement

The parent item (AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6) shipped the pure power-up level model —
`POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`, `resolvePowerUpAtLevel()` and a run-scoped
`PowerUpLevelStore` (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`) — and the hold-full choice
integration (AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9). The model is **not yet consumed by the effect
path**: `EffectsRegistry` still uses raw tuning constants (`P5_SPEED_MULTIPLIER`,
`P3_SHIELD_DURATION`, `P8_LIVES_MAX`, `P9_MAX_STACKS`, `P10_MAX_STACKS`, …) and
tracks its own independent counters (`_magnetStacks`, `_scoopStacks`,
`_teleportStacks`, `_phaseCharges`, `_lives`). Field pickups never touch the
level store at all, so a power-up only levels when a hold-full choice is spent
on it — contradicting the producer-confirmed "every collection levels the
power-up up" (parent Q1=A). The result is three defects: (1) a hold-full
`power-up-level` summary can promise a delta the effect path never applies,
(2) two parallel state models can drift/double-count, and (3) the game and the
gyms can diverge.

## Users

- **Player (progression parity):** "As a player, every power-up I collect should
  measurably strengthen it for the rest of the run, exactly as weapons do, so
  field drops and hold-full picks both matter."
- **Player (trustworthy choice):** "As a player, the change summary on a
  power-up level-up must be the change I actually get in play."
- **Developer:** "As a developer, I want one run-scoped level store consumed
  identically by `EffectsRegistry`, `PlayScene` and every gym, so power-up
  strength cannot diverge between scenes."
- **Designer/tuner:** "As a designer, I want the effect path to read the
  catalogue (one source of truth), so balance intent cannot drift from the
  numbers scattered through scenes."

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` (P3–P10, each with
  `base`/`cap`/`k`/`discrete`/`rationale`), pure `resolvePowerUpAtLevel()`, the
  pure `summarisePowerUpLevelChange()`, and the run-scoped `PowerUpLevelStore`
  (`collect`, `getLevel`, `getUpgradeLevel`, `getLevels`, `stats`,
  `magnetStacks`, `scoopStacks`, `teleportStacks`, `consumeTeleport`,
  `phaseCharges`, `isPhasePermanent`, `consumePhaseCharge`, `lives`, `reset`).
  The store already derives P9/P10 permanent stacks, P7 teleports, P6 charges
  and P8 lives, and its `collect()` already adds the resolved per-pickup grants.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — owns `_powerUpLevelStore: PowerUpLevelStore`;
  exposes `collectPowerUp`, `getPowerUpLevel`, `getPowerUpLevels`,
  `resetPowerUpLevels`. The choice launchers read `player.getPowerUpLevels()`.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `EffectsRegistry` holds the **parallel** effect
  state: `_timed` (P3/P5/P6/P9/P10 timed), `_lives`, `_magnetStacks`,
  `_scoopStacks`, `_teleportStacks`, `_weapons`, `_phaseCharges`,
  `_phasePermanent`, `_phaseDangerCleared`, `_phaseRearmCooldown`. It reads raw
  constants; it never calls the level store.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `_collectDrop()` applies a field
  pickup with `registry.applyCollect(drop.dropId)` (no `player.collectPowerUp`).
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — `applyMineralChoiceReward()` applies a
  hold-full pick with `registry.applyCollect(id, true)` **and**
  `player.collectPowerUp(id, true)` (two stores, incremented once each).
- GDD §4.4.3 documents the model and states explicitly that "wiring the resolver
  into `EffectsRegistry`/scenes and the gym parity demonstration ship in
  follow-up items". README §Key files carries the same note.

## Design recommendation (agent recommendation — Q1/Q2 pending)

1. **Single store, owned by `Player`, consumed by `EffectsRegistry`.** The store
   already backs the shipped choice integration (`player.getPowerUpLevels()`),
   so it stays owned by `Player`. `EffectsRegistry` is handed **that same
   instance** (constructor parameter defaulting to a private store for
   standalone use/tests; scenes wire the player's store in). This is the only
   way "no double-counting / no separate counters" (parent AC3) holds.
2. **`EffectsRegistry.applyCollect()` becomes the single mutation point.** It
   calls `store.collect(id, permanent)` (advancing the level and the derived
   grants once) and then resolves the effect from `store.stats(id)`. The
   registry's duplicate counters and their accessors delegate to the store
   (`_phaseDangerCleared` / `_phaseRearmCooldown` stay in the registry — they
   are timing state, not level state). The hold-full path
   (`applyMineralChoiceReward`) drops its explicit `player.collectPowerUp(...)`
   call so the shared store is not advanced twice.
3. **Field pickups need no extra call.** Because `applyCollect()` now advances
   the shared store, the existing `_collectDrop()` path levels the power-up up
   automatically — the same code in the game and every gym.
4. **Resolved stats replace raw constants.** Durations (P3 `shieldDuration`,
   P5 `speedDuration`, P6 `phaseDuration`, P7 `teleportPhaseDuration`), the P5
   `speedMultiplier`, P6 `phaseCharges`, P7 `teleportStacks`, P8 `lifeGain` /
   `livesCap` and P9/P10 stack caps are read from the resolver. The P9/P10
   **field-pickup** timed durations (15 s) are **not** a catalogue axis and stay
   as constants (documented), unless the producer decides otherwise.
5. **Run-scoped reset.** `reset()` clears the store (levels + derived
   resources) and the registry's timing state together, so a restart returns
   both to base — matching the existing restart/teardown parity work.

## Desired change

Wire the resolver/store into `EffectsRegistry` and the shared effect path;
remove the duplicate counters in favour of the store; make `applyCollect`
advance the level exactly once; resolve effect strength from the catalogue;
keep the P9/P10 hybrid intact; wire the same path into `PlayScene` and every
gym; update the GDD/README and tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Single run-scoped level store.** `EffectsRegistry` consumes the same
  `PowerUpLevelStore` instance as `Player`; there is no second, independently
  incremented counter. Every collection (field pickup **or** hold-full reward)
  increments the level exactly once; the level persists across a timed
  activation expiring and resets only on run restart.
- **AC2 — Resolved stats replace raw constants.** Effect durations, the P5
  multiplier, per-pickup grants and caps are read from
  `resolvePowerUpAtLevel()`/`store.stats()`; `P5_SPEED_MULTIPLIER`,
  `P3_SHIELD_DURATION`, `P8_LIVES_MAX`, `P9_MAX_STACKS` and `P10_MAX_STACKS`
  are no longer the source of truth for effect strength. Any non-levelled
  constant that remains (P9/P10 field-pickup 15 s) is documented as such.
- **AC3 — Stack/charge/lives reconciliation.** P9/P10 permanent stacks, P7
  stored teleports, P6 charges and P8 lives are derived from the level store
  with no separate counters and no double-counting; the P9/P10 hybrid is
  preserved (a field pickup levels up and refreshes the timed attraction but
  adds no permanent stack).
- **AC4 — P3/P4 level-axis consumption.** *(Blocked on Q2.)* Either (a) P3
  shield absorbs up to the resolved `shieldAbsorptions` before popping and P4
  banks/consumes the resolved `bombCharges` through a defined trigger, or
  (b) these two axes are explicitly deferred to a new child work item while the
  level store still tracks them. Either way a hold-full `power-up-level` summary
